# ethereum-optimism/ecosystem Daily Update (Aug 27, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
Today's focus was on repository cleanup and interop compatibility. Key activities included assessing documentation links for archiving, analyzing starter repo consolidation, and addressing a critical sequencer wedge issue.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

No completed work was reported for this day.

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
- **Documentation Updates**: A new pull request, [#1019](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/pull/1019), was opened to update the `README` with supported surface information.
- **Cleanup of Superseded Applications**: Another pull request, [#1018](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/pull/1018), was opened to remove the `autorelayer-interop` application, as it has been superseded.

## CLOSED ISSUES

- **Supernode Interop Stability**: Issue [#22325](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/22325), concerning `op-supernode` cross-safe wedges after invalid-message replacement, was closed. The issue was identified as a single occurrence in 7.5 weeks, with the root cause traced to chain 901 rejecting batches due to a parent-hash mismatch, pointing to an oscillation issue rather than a distinct cross-safety bug.
- **Kona Genesis Configuration Leniency**: Issue [#22682](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/22682), regarding `RollupConfig` silently accepting unknown `rollup.json` keys in Kona, was closed as "not planned." The leniency is deliberate to support retired keys, and the superchain-registry config tests cover fields not yet modeled by Kona.

## NEW ISSUES

- **SuperchainERC20 Compatibility Checking**: A new issue, [#1020](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/1020), was created to address the lack of a supported way for developers to check if a token address is SuperchainERC20 compatible. This capability was previously part of an archived repository and needs a new home.

## ACTIVE ISSUES

- **Starter Examples Documentation Audit**: Issue [#1014](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/1014) is active, with a comprehensive reference map completed. The audit found no live documentation links to any of the six starter repos or four archive-sweep repos, meaning archiving will not break published docs. The blast radius for README cross-references is self-contained, with only three external fix-up items identified. The issue also noted that `ethereum-optimism/docs` is still linked in two places in live docs despite being archived.
- **Starter Examples Consolidation**: Issue [#1015](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/1015) is active, with a migration analysis recommending consolidating five `superchain-starter*` repos into `superchain-starter`, while leaving `superchainerc20-starter` independent due to its distinct nature and popularity. The recommendation is to use a plain copy with a pointer to the original for history preservation. The execution is currently blocked by the need for write access to several repositories and org admin privileges for archiving.
- **Abandoned and Dead Repos Archiving**: Issue [#1017](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/1017) is active, with an inbound-link check completed for four target repos (`superchainerc20-compatibility`, `optimism-starter`, `scaffold-op`, `optimism-mud-starter`). No live documentation links any of these repos. The total fix-up work involves two README edits. The capability of `superchainerc20-compatibility` (checking token interop compatibility) has been captured in a new issue [#1020](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/1020). Archiving is currently blocked by permissions.
- **Kona Node NetworkActor Stalls**: Issue [#22646](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/22646) is active, discussing how `NetworkActor` can stall the p2p swarm during remote-signer HTTP calls. A developer has offered to pick up the issue and raised questions about overflow policy and whether to land the deadline change separately from other restructuring. They plan to confirm the stall by running a Kona node sequencer against a signer with injected latency.
- **Kona Node Sequencer Wedge**: Issue [#22681](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/22681) describes a critical problem where a Kona node sequencer can get permanently wedged in a `forkchoiceUpdated` loop. A related fix in [#22686](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/pull/22686) addresses the reported wedge, but three pre-existing gaps remain: `SealTask` errors not triggering a reset, `QueuedSequencerEngineClient`'s `recv().await` calls lacking timeouts, and the sequencer's next parent coming from a lagging watch channel.
